key_insight: AMIFound is a single foundation model that can restore and enhance medical images from seven different imaging modalities. It improves image quality across diverse degradations while preserving clinically important details needed for diagnosis.
problem_solved: Medical images often suffer from noise, blur, low contrast, motion artifacts, and other degradations, but existing restoration methods are usually specialized for one modality or one type of corruption. This paper addresses the need for a unified model that works robustly across multiple modalities and degradation types.
method: Builds a multimodal foundation model trained to handle medical image restoration and enhancement across seven imaging modalities.
Learns general restoration capabilities that transfer across different degradation patterns instead of relying on modality-specific models.
Emphasizes preserving diagnostic information so enhanced images remain clinically useful.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows a scalable path toward one model for many medical imaging restoration tasks, reducing the need to maintain separate pipelines. It also highlights how foundation models can improve robustness and clinical utility in real-world healthcare workflows.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing degraded medical images flowing into AMIFound and emerging as restored/enhanced outputs.

paper_title: An all-in-one foundation model for multimodal medical image restoration and enhancement
paper_authors: Luyang Cao, Zhijian Wu, Jian Zhang, Lei Qi, Yang Gao
